To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) ubiquitin ligases represent key players in cancer formation; (2) the ubiquitin system is a major target for the design of cancer therapies; and (3) E3 ubiquitin genes are promising targets for mutation screenings and for the identification of new cancer susceptibility genes.
E3 ubiquitylation enzymes represent a large and diverse group of enzymes that play an essential role in the regulation of cell cycle, apoptosis, DNA repair, and other important cellular processes.

ubiquitin ligases, which are enzymes that tag proteins for degradation, are over‐represented in cancer.
